criteria.text: The response identifies that Section 10 of the Confirmatory IP Assignment Agreement selects Delaware law and the exclusive jurisdiction of the Delaware Court of Chancery. It also identifies that this conflicts with SPA Section 11.8, which selects New York law and New York County courts as the exclusive forum. It recognises that under SPA Section 11.10 the IP Assignment Agreement controls as to its subject matter, so the SPA does not cure the conflict. It explains why this matters to Breidoun and recommends a fix.
hints: Court of Chancery of the State of Delaware

criteria.text: The response identifies that the Key Employee Agreement (Section 1 and/or Section 7) defines "Business" as only the preparation of hot inflight meals. It identifies that this is narrower than the SPA Section 1.1 definition, which also covers galley provisioning and crew meal services. It concludes that Solvig's non-compete leaves those service lines unprotected. It explains why this matters to Breidoun and recommends a fix.
hints: galley provisioning and crew meal services

criteria.text: The response identifies that under SPA Section 2.4(b) the 30-day window to deliver a Notice of Disagreement ran from the August 3, 2026 delivery of the Closing Statement and expired on or about September 2, 2026. It concludes that Breidoun's September 18, 2026 notice is late and that the Closing Statement risks becoming final and binding. It explains why this matters to Breidoun and recommends a fix.

The response identifies that Section 8.3 of the Confirmatory IP Assignment Agreement subjects Seller's liability for breach of the SPA Section 4.12 IP representations to the SPA Section 9.5(a) cap, notwithstanding Section 9.5(b). It concludes that this removes the carve-out for IP representation breaches, so IP losses are now capped at 10% of the Purchase Price. It explains why this matters to Breidoun and recommends a fix.
The response states that the Stock Purchase Agreement is governed by New York law.
The response states that the SPA indemnity cap is 10% of the Purchase Price.
The response states that the SPA defines "Business" to include inflight catering, galley provisioning and crew meal services for regional air carriers.
hints: inflight catering, galley provisioning and crew meal services

criteria.text: The response is a memo that lists the issues separately. For each issue it gives the document and section, and it orders the issues so that those it presents as highest risk to the client come first.
The response states a conclusion on whether anything in the linen and galley-cart washing services agreement matters for Breidoun.
The response claims that Breidoun's September 18, 2026 Notice of Disagreement was delivered within the SPA's 30-day window.
The response claims that the SPA's New York governing law and forum clause overrides the IP Assignment Agreement's Delaware clause as to IP matters.
